jonny-desktop.task: context-keeper: verify entries against a commit SHA rather than a timestamp, so drift is exact under clock skew, rebases and amended commits
jonny-desktop.note: DONE + PUSHED + PR OPEN, CI GREEN, AWAITING MERGE. context-keeper PR #12 on feat/verify-against-sha, 4/4 green. 361 tests, up from 354. Entries now carry verified_sha, stamped SERVER-SIDE at every point verified_at is set (three record paths, update_entry, and the dedup merge - the merge path needed base_dir threaded through _merge_entry_fields, which the existing tests caught as a NameError). Deliberately not a tool parameter: it is an observation about the machine doing the write, not something a caller should assert, and keeping it off the schema keeps tools/list unchanged at ~2955 against con-004's 195 tokens of headroom. Comparison stays inside the single git log: each commit carries its index and newest-first ordering means a commit is after the verified point exactly when it sits at a lower index, so there is still no per-entry spawn. TWO FALLBACKS, both tested: a SHA that no longer resolves (rebased away, amended, shallow clone) degrades to the timestamp rather than crashing or silently reporting zero, and entries predating the feature take the same path; the report exposes verified_against sha|timestamp so an exact answer stays distinguishable from a best-effort one. A TEST CAUGHT A CIRCULAR DESIGN FLAW: the git window is derived from timestamps, so it could fail to contain the very commit the SHA names - and that bites exactly when the timestamp is wrong, which is the whole reason for preferring the SHA. An entry with a future verified_at produced an empty window and reported zero drift while one real commit sat there. Fixed by widening once, bounded by MAX_COMMITS, only when a given SHA is missing; measured at 1 git log in the common case and 2 in the fallback. All 7 new tests fail against the previous implementation, covering both directions of the clock problem (past timestamp over-reports, future timestamp hides drift entirely). This closes the full improvement list: drift, scope resolution, usage tracking, passive capture, task-aware injection, enforced_by, SHA verification.
